mainTopic: Shrinking an oversized קרפף, partitions on top of partitions (for שבת and for acquiring a גר's property), and whether a roofed area counts toward a קרפף's size
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier מחלוקת about carrying where there are no דיורין (residents). The גמרא then asks how to shrink a קרפף larger than בית סאתים so that carrying becomes permitted. Trees do not count. A column 4 טפחים wide, or a new partition set 4 טפחים back from the wall, does count. For the 3-to-4 טפחים range, רבה says it works because it is beyond לבוד, and רבא says it does not because it is not a מקום ארבעה. רב שימי reports a version where they argue only about plaster that cannot stand on its own. Next comes a partition built at a mound's edge, which is a 'partition on top of a partition.' The גמרא proves that רב חסדא holds it works for שבת, though it does not acquire a גר's property, while רב ששת says it does not work even for שבת. רבה בר בר חנה asks what happens if the lower walls sink. The גמרא argues the answer is already known both for acquiring property (the turnip case) and for שבת (a ברייתא about partitions made on שבת, with רב נחמן's limit applying only to מזיד). A story of רב נחמן ruling against a woman's partition on a partition follows. Finally, רבא and רבי זירא argue whether a roofed section adds to a קרפף's size, and the גמרא suggests linking this to רב and שמואל's dispute over פי תקרה יורד וסותם.

steps.title: Reasons behind the permitting and forbidding opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains both sides of the previous מחלוקת. The one who permits says there are no residents there. The one who forbids worries that sometimes there will be residents and people will carry out of habit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who permits holds this way because there are no residents there. The one who forbids holds this way because sometimes there are residents in it, and people will come to carry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a מחלוקת from the previous lines by giving each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who permits looks at the situation right now: with no דיורין in the place, nobody there can make carrying forbidden. The one who forbids looks ahead: at times there will be residents. People who are used to carrying freely might then keep carrying when it is actually אסור. So he forbids it even now, as a protective גזירה.
steps.whatToRemember: The permitter looks at the present (no דיורין). The forbidder adds a protective concern for the future (sometimes there will be דיורין, and people may carry by habit).
steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the earlier discussion, not to the קרפף topic that comes next. Do not read it as part of the reduction cases.

phrases.english: The one who permits — because there are no residents.
And the one who forbids —
sometimes there are residents in it
and they will come to carry.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאן דשרי — דהא ליכא דיורין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind a מחלוקת stated on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permitter: no דיורין, so nothing forbids carrying. Forbidder: residents are sometimes present, so carrying is forbidden as a safeguard.

steps.title: Planting trees does not reduce an oversized enclosure
steps.stepSummary: A קרפף larger than בית סאתים that was not fenced for living may be shrunk to make it permitted. Planting trees in it does not count as shrinking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קרפף larger than בית סאתים that was not enclosed for living, and someone wants to make it smaller: if he made it smaller with trees, that is not a reduction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how to shrink an oversized קרפף so that carrying inside it becomes permitted. Its first rule is that trees do not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרפף bigger than בית סאתים that was not enclosed for living is treated like a כרמלית, so carrying in it is forbidden. Shrinking it to בית סאתים or less would solve this. But trees are a normal part of a yard used for living. They do not change the space, so they do not take any area away from it.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed area outside the house, like a storage yard
An area the size of two סאה of seed, 5,000 square אמות (the size of the משכן courtyard)
Enclosed for the purpose of living there
A reduction (valid shrinking of the area)

steps.confusionAlert: The goal is to make the קרפף SMALLER, not bigger. The limit of בית סאתים is the maximum size allowed for carrying in an area not enclosed for living.

phrases.english: A karpef larger than two beit se'a
that was not enclosed for residence
and one came to reduce it,
if he reduced it with trees — it is not a reduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: קרפף יותר מבית סאתים שלא הוקף לדירה ובא למעטו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic; not connected to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trees do not count as a מיעוט of an oversized קרפף.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the question the rest of this passage answers: what kind of object does count as shrinking the area?

steps.title: A column ten high and four wide reduces; under three does not
steps.stepSummary: A column 10 טפחים high and 4 wide counts as a reduction. A column narrower than 3 טפחים does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he built in it a column ten טפחים high and four wide, it is a reduction. If it is less than three, it is not a reduction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the clear cases at both ends: a column 4 טפחים wide definitely shrinks the area, and one under 3 definitely does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A column 10 טפחים high and 4 wide is a significant structure of its own, a רשות in its own right, so its area is taken out of the קרפף. A column under 3 wide is too small to matter. This leaves an open middle case, between 3 and 4, which the next step takes up.

phrases.english: If he built in it a column ten handbreadths high
and four wide — it is a reduction.
Less than three — it is not a reduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: בנה בו עמוד גבוה עשרה ורחב ארבעה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 2: unlike trees, a proper column does reduce the area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A column 10 high by 4 wide is a מיעוט. A column under 3 wide is not.

steps.title: Dispute about a column between three and four wide
steps.stepSummary: For a column 3 to 4 טפחים wide, רבה says it counts as a reduction and רבא says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From three to four: רבה said it is a reduction, and רבא said it is not a reduction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a מחלוקת between רבה and רבא about the middle case left open in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the cases at the edges (4 or more counts, under 3 does not). They disagree only on the in-between width. The next two steps explain each side's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: From three up to four טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רבא are two different people with almost the same spelling. Here רבה says it counts and רבא says it does not.

phrases.english: From three up to four —
Rabba said: it is a reduction,
and Rava said: it is not a reduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: משלשה ועד ארבעה — רבה אמר הוי מיעוט ורבא אמר לא הוי מיעוט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up the middle case left open by step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: a column 3 to 4 wide is a מיעוט. רבא: it is not.

steps.title: רבה's reason: it is beyond the rule of לבוד
steps.stepSummary: רבה holds that a column 3 or more wide counts as a reduction because it is no longer covered by the rule of לבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said it is a reduction, because it has left the rule of לבוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבה's view in order to explain his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under לבוד, anything less than 3 טפחים is treated as if it is not there as a separate thing; a gap that small is seen as closed. Once the column is 3 or more wide, לבוד no longer swallows it. For רבה, that makes it a real object of its own, and so it shrinks the area.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule that a gap under 3 טפחים is treated as closed or joined
It goes out of the category or rule of

phrases.english: Rabba said: it is a reduction,
since it has left the category of lavud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבה אמר הוי מיעוט דהא נפיק ליה מתורת לבוד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the מחלוקת in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבה, being 3 טפחים wide or more, beyond לבוד, is enough to make the column count.

steps.title: רבא's reason: under four is not significant
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that a column narrower than 4 טפחים does not count as a reduction, because it is not a מקום ארבעה and so is not significant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said it is not a reduction: since it is not a place of four, it is not significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבא's view in order to explain his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, getting past לבוד is not enough. To count as a real space of its own, an area must be at least 4 by 4 טפחים (a מקום ארבעה). A column narrower than that is not חשיב, significant, so it does not take any area out of the קרפף.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of four by four טפחים, the minimum for a significant space

steps.whatToRemember: רבה uses the 3-טפח line of לבוד, so a column of 3 or more counts. רבא uses the 4-טפח line of a significant place, so a column must be 4 to count.

phrases.english: Rava said: it is not a reduction,
since it is not a place of four —
it is not significant.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמר לא הוי מיעוט כיון דלא הוי מקום ארבעה לא חשיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second side of the מחלוקת, in contrast to רבה's reason in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבא, only a column that is a מקום ארבעה (4 טפחים wide) is significant enough to count as a מיעוט.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two different measuring lines in הלכה: 3 טפחים (the line of לבוד) and 4 טפחים (the line of a significant place).

steps.title: A new partition built a distance from the wall
steps.stepSummary: If someone builds a new partition 4 טפחים away from the old wall of the קרפף, it works to shrink the area. If it is less than 3 away, it does not work. Between 3 and 4, רבה says it works and רבא says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he moved four טפחים away from the wall and built a partition, it works. If it is less than three, it does not work. From three up to four: רבה said it works, and רבא said it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case with the same pattern as the column case. Here a person builds a new partition inside the קרפף, set back from the old wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new partition makes the usable area smaller, so the קרפף may now be small enough to be permitted. At 4 טפחים or more, everyone agrees it counts. At less than 3, the gap is so small that the new partition is treated as stuck to the old wall, so nothing was really shrunk. The gap of 3 to 4 is the same zone where רבה and רבא argued about the column.

keyTerms.meaning: he moved away / set it at a distance
wall (the original wall of the קרפף)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new topic. It is a second example of the exact same 3 to 4 טפחים dispute you just learned about the column, now applied to a partition.

phrases.english: If he moved four handbreadths away from the wall
phrases.notes: The wall of the oversized קרפף.

phrases.english: and built a partition, it is effective.
Less than three, it is not effective.
phrases.notes: Because of לבוד, it counts as attached to the old wall.

phrases.english: From three up to four:
Rabba said: it is effective,
Rava said: it is not effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִרְחִיק מִן הַכּוֹתֶל אַרְבָּעָה וְעָשָׂה מְחִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the column pattern from steps 3 to 6 to a new case, a partition set back from the wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partition 4 טפחים from the wall reduces the area. One less than 3 away does not. At 3 to 4, רבה says it works and רבא says it does not.

steps.title: רבה's reason: the partition is outside the rule of לבוד
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the partition works because at 3 טפחים or more it is no longer treated as attached to the old wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said it works, because it has left the rule of לבוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבה holds that a partition 3 to 4 טפחים from the wall works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לבוד treats a gap smaller than 3 טפחים as if it were closed. Once the gap is 3 or more, the new partition is a separate wall that truly cuts off space. This is the same reasoning רבה gave for the column in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: the rule of לבוד (a gap under 3 טפחים counts as closed)

phrases.english: Rabba said: it is effective,
because it has left the rule of lavud.
phrases.notes: At 3 or more, it is not considered joined to the old wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא נָפֵיק לֵיהּ מִתּוֹרַת לָבוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבה's position in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the gap is 3 טפחים or more, לבוד no longer applies, so the partition is a real reduction.

steps.title: רבא's reason: a space under 4 טפחים is not significant
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the partition does not work because the space it cuts off is less than 4 טפחים, so it does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said it does not work, because since it is not a space of four, it is not significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא holds that a partition only 3 to 4 טפחים from the wall does not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, escaping לבוד is not enough. The strip of space that was cut off must be at least 4 טפחים, a מקום ארבעה, to count as a real space. A strip narrower than that is ignored, so the קרפף is treated as not shrunk.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not significant / it does not count

steps.whatToRemember: In the partition case, as with the column: 4 or more works, under 3 does not, and at 3 to 4 רבה says it works (it is outside לבוד) while רבא says it does not (it is not a מקום ארבעה).

phrases.english: Rava said: it is not effective,
since it is not a place of four,
it is not significant.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוֵי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה לָא חֲשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבא's position in step 7, which is the opposite of רבה's in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cut-off space smaller than 4 טפחים is not significant, so the partition does not reduce the קרפף.

steps.title: רב שימי's lenient version: plastering the wall
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי teaches the dispute differently. If someone thickens the wall with plaster that can stand on its own, it counts as shrinking. If the plaster cannot stand on its own, רבה says it counts and רבא says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי taught it in a lenient way: if he smeared plaster on it and the plaster can stand on its own, it counts as a reduction. If it cannot stand on its own, רבה said it counts as a reduction, and רבא said it does not count as a reduction.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא, רב שימי, reports a different version of what רבה and רבא argued about. In his version they argue about plaster added to the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick plaster on the wall takes up a little of the area, so the קרפף becomes slightly smaller. If the plaster could stand even without the wall, everyone agrees it counts. The argument is only about plaster that stays up only because it is stuck to the wall. This version is called "lenient" because it places the dispute in a weaker case, which suggests that in the stronger cases, such as the column and the partition, everyone agrees the reduction works.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches it in the lenient direction
smeared plaster or mud on it (the wall)

steps.confusionAlert: רב שימי is not adding a third opinion. He is reporting a different version of where the רבה and רבא dispute took place, and his version is the more lenient one overall.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi would teach it leniently:
If he smeared plaster on it
phrases.notes: On the wall of the oversized קרפף.

phrases.aramaic: וְיָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ — הָוֵי מִיעוּט.
phrases.english: and it can stand on its own, it is a reduction.
If it cannot stand on its own:
Rabba said: it is a reduction,
Rava said: it is not a reduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי מַתְנֵי לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative version of the רבה and רבא dispute, moving it from the column and partition cases to the plaster case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plaster that can stand by itself reduces the קרפף. For plaster that cannot stand by itself, רבה says it reduces the area and רבא says it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: By placing the dispute in a weaker case, this version suggests that in the column and partition cases both רבה and רבא would agree the reduction works.

steps.title: רבה's reason: right now, the plaster is standing
steps.stepSummary: רבה says even weak plaster counts, because at this moment it is in fact standing there and taking up space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said it is a reduction, because right now, at least, it is standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבה counts plaster that cannot stand on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה looks at the present reality. The plaster is there now and fills part of the area, so the קרפף really is smaller. It does not matter that the plaster would fall without the wall.

phrases.english: Rabba said: it is a reduction,
since now, at any rate, it is standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבה's position in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What matters is that the plaster is standing now, so it reduces the area.

steps.title: רבא's reason: plaster that cannot stand alone is nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבא says plaster that cannot stand by itself counts for nothing, so it does not shrink the קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said it is not a reduction, because since it cannot stand on its own, it is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא does not count plaster that cannot stand on its own, and this closes the רב שימי version of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, something that only stays up by leaning on the wall has no standing of its own. It is treated as if it were not there, so the size of the קרפף has not changed.

keyTerms.meaning: it is nothing / it does not count at all

steps.whatToRemember: In רב שימי's version, everyone agrees that plaster which can stand by itself counts. For plaster that cannot stand by itself, רבה says it counts because it stands right now, and רבא says it is nothing because it cannot stand alone.

phrases.english: Rava said: it is not a reduction,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא יָכוֹל לְמֵיקַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: since it cannot stand on its own,
it is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא יָכוֹל לְמֵיקַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ לֹא כְּלוּם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבא's position in step 10, which is the opposite of רבה's in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plaster that cannot stand on its own is insignificant and does not reduce the קרפף.

steps.title: A partition built four טפחים from the mound works
steps.stepSummary: If a person builds a new partition 4 טפחים away from a high mound in a large קרפף, the partition is effective.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he moved 4 טפחים away from the mound and built a partition, it works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a clear rule: a new partition placed 4 טפחים away from the mound is effective. This is the simple case that sets up the harder case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mound is 10 טפחים high, so it already acts like a wall, but it was not made for living. A new partition 4 טפחים away is clearly its own separate wall, built for living, so it fixes the area for carrying. This matches the earlier discussion of 3 and 4 טפחים from רבה and רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A mound or raised heap of earth (here 10 טפחים high, acting like a wall)

phrases.english: If he distanced himself four (handbreadths) from the mound
phrases.notes: The mound is 10 טפחים high and stands inside a קרפף larger than בית סאתים.

phrases.english: and made a partition — it is effective.
phrases.notes: The new partition is built for the purpose of living, so carrying becomes permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִרְחִיק מִן הַתֵּל אַרְבָּעָה וְעָשָׂה מְחִיצָה הוֹעִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the plaster dispute to a new but related case: a mound acting as a wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new partition 4 טפחים away from the mound is effective.

steps.title: Dispute when the partition is very close to the mound
steps.stepSummary: If the partition is less than 3 טפחים from the mound, or right on its edge, רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree whether it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is less than 3 טפחים away, or on the very edge of the mound, רב חסדא and רב המנונא argue. One says it works, and one says it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the harder case: the new partition is almost touching the mound. Two אמוראים argue, but we are not told who holds which side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Less than 3 טפחים counts as attached to the mound, so the new partition is like a wall built on top of an old wall. The question is whether such a 'wall on a wall' counts as a real new partition. The unclear 'one said, one said' sets up the next step, which figures out who said what.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than three (טפחים); close enough to count as attached
One said... and the other said (opinions not yet assigned)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the first name (רב חסדא) goes with the first opinion ('it works'). The phrase 'חד אמר... וחד אמר' means we do not yet know who said what. The next step works that out.

phrases.english: Less than three (handbreadths)
phrases.notes: Counts as touching the mound, so it is like a partition on top of a partition.

phrases.english: or on the edge of the mound,
Rav Ḥisda and Rav Hamnuna (disagree):
one said: it is effective,
and the other said: it is not effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא חַד אָמַר הוֹעִיל וְחַד אָמַר לֹא הוֹעִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the clear 4-טפחים case with the unclear close-up case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partition less than 3 טפחים from the mound, or on its edge, is disputed: one אמורא says it works, one says it does not.

steps.title: Proving that רב חסדא is the one who says it works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רב חסדא holds 'it works,' because he ruled elsewhere that a partition on top of a partition works for שבת, though not for acquiring a convert's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רב חסדא is the one who said it works. For it was taught: if someone builds a partition on top of another partition, רב חסדא said: for שבת it works, but for the property of a convert he does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles who said what in the previous dispute. It quotes another ruling of רב חסדא that matches the 'it works' side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partition at the mound's edge is just like a partition on top of a partition, and רב חסדא already said that works for שבת. For שבת, what matters is having a wall made for living, and the new wall gives that. But for taking ownership of an ownerless convert's land, the land was already walled in, so adding another wall is not a real act of taking possession (חזקה).

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude / it can be proven (used to assign opinions)
For it was stated (introduces an אמורא teaching)
The property of a convert (ownerless if he died with no heirs)

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא holds that a partition built at the edge of the mound (a 'wall on a wall') works for שבת, so רב המנונא is the one who says it does not work. The same wall does not count as an act of acquisition for a convert's property.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one physical act can count for one area of הלכה (walls for שבת) but not for another (acquiring land), because each area asks a different question.

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rav Ḥisda who said it is effective,
for it was stated: one who makes a partition
on top of a partition,
Rav Ḥisda said: for Shabbat, it is effective.
phrases.notes: For example, when the first partition was not made for living.

phrases.english: With the property of a convert, he does not acquire.
phrases.notes: A new wall on top of an existing wall is not a valid act of taking possession of ownerless land.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר הוֹעִיל דְּאִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the unassigned dispute from step 14 by bringing another teaching of רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: That רב חסדא is the אמורא who holds a partition at the mound's edge is effective.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's ruling that a partition on top of a partition is effective for שבת, though it does not acquire a convert's property.

steps.title: רב ששת disagrees, so the 'it works' opinion belongs to רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says a partition on top of a partition does not work even for שבת. So the גמרא concludes that רב חסדא is the one who holds it works for שבת, which means he also holds that a partition near the mound works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: even for שבת it also does not work. Conclude from this (that רב חסדא is the one who says it works).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the argument quoted in Step 15. Then it closes the proof with the word תסתיים, meaning 'yes, we can conclude it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15 we saw an opinion that a partition on top of a partition works for שבת but not for acquiring a convert's property. Here we learn that רב ששת rejects even the שבת part. That leaves רב חסדא as the one who says it works for שבת, so in our mound case רב חסדא must be the one who says 'it works.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is not effective / it does not work

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: a partition on top of a partition works for שבת. רב ששת: it does not work, even for שבת.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
Even regarding Shabbat it also is not effective.
phrases.notes: A partition on top of an existing partition does not count at all.

phrases.english: Conclude (that Rav Chisda is the one who says it works).
phrases.notes: The proof from Step 15 is accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof started in Step 15 by giving רב ששת's opposing view, then concludes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the dispute about a partition near or at the edge of the mound, רב חסדא is the one who says it works, and רב המנונא says it does not.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רב ששת agrees that a partition on top of the mound works
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that רב ששת agrees with him in one case. If someone builds a partition on top of the mound itself, it works for carrying on the mound.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: רב ששת agrees with me that if a person built a partition on the mound, it is effective.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא points to a case where even his opponent רב ששת agrees: partitions built up on top of the mound do work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally רב ששת says a partition on top of a partition does not work. But here the new walls stand on the mound itself. For the area on top of the mound they serve a real purpose, even though, according to רב ששת, they still do not fix the rest of the קרפף below.

keyTerms.meaning: A mound, a raised area whose sides act as natural partitions

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not changing his opinion. The new partitions help only for carrying on top of the mound. They do not help for the large קרפף below.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
And Rav Sheshet agrees with me
that if one made a partition on the mound,
phrases.notes: Built on top of the mound, not just next to it.

phrases.english: that it is effective.
phrases.notes: It works for carrying on the mound itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה לִי רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting up the dispute, רב חסדא names a case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partition built on top of the mound works for carrying on the mound, even according to רב ששת.

steps.title: Why does רב ששת agree here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that even רב ששת agrees in the case of a partition on the mound.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא is preparing to explain רב ששת's agreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an apparent problem: רב ששת says a partition on top of a partition does not work. A wall on the mound looks just like that, so the גמרא needs to explain why it works here.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind רב חסדא's claim in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב ששת accepts a partition on top of the mound when he rejects partitions on top of partitions.

steps.title: Because he lives inside the space of the upper walls
steps.stepSummary: The person on top of the mound lives within the airspace enclosed by the new upper partitions, so those walls serve him and count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he lives in the airspace of the upper partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. For someone up on the mound, the new walls are the walls that actually surround him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From below, the new walls are just extra walls stacked on the mound's sides, and that is why רב ששת says they do not help the קרפף. From on top of the mound, they are the only walls enclosing the person's space. Because they really serve him, they count for carrying on the mound.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper partitions, the ones built on top of the mound

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether a partition counts depends on whether it actually encloses and serves the space where the person is.

phrases.english: Since in the airspace of the upper partitions
he dwells.
phrases.notes: So for him, these are real, working walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וּבַאֲוִיר מְחִיצוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת הוּא דָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The upper partitions surround the space where the person on the mound lives, so they function for him.

steps.title: What if the lower partitions sink and only the upper ones remain?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה asks about a case where the mound's lower partitions sank into the ground but the upper partitions built on top are still standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה asked: if the lower partitions were swallowed up and the upper ones still stand, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבה בר בר חנה asks whether the upper walls now count once the lower walls under them are gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper walls were weak at first only because they stood on top of other partitions. Now the lower partitions have disappeared, for example by sinking into soft ground, and the upper walls remain. The question is whether the upper walls now count as real partitions, or whether they stay invalid because they were invalid when they were built.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question / raised a dilemma
Were swallowed up, sank into the ground
The lower partitions, the original sides of the mound

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana asked:
If the lower partitions were swallowed up,
phrases.notes: For example, they sank into boggy ground.

phrases.english: and the upper ones still stand,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea of upper partitions on top of lower ones and asks about a new case where the lower ones are gone.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether upper partitions that were invalid as a 'partition on a partition' become valid once the lower partitions disappear.

steps.title: What area of law is the question about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical issue רבה בר בר חנה's question concerns.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose was this asked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of law the question about the sunken partitions is really about. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא tests two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same physical case could matter for two different areas of law. The גמרא wants to know which one, because each area may already have a known answer. If so, the question would be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose? About what issue?

phrases.english: With regard to what?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the context of רבה בר בר חנה's question from Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which area of law (property acquisition or שבת) the question about the sunken partitions concerns.

steps.title: If it is about a convert's property, it is already known
steps.stepSummary: If the question is about acquiring a convert's property, the גמרא says ירמיה ביראה's ruling already settles it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about the property of a convert, this is the same as the ruling of ירמיה ביראה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that the question concerns acquiring ownerless property, and says this is already answered by a known ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A convert who dies without Jewish heirs leaves property that belongs to no one, and anyone can acquire it by doing an act of improvement such as building a fence. If the lower walls sink, the upper walls now become the 'fence' without anyone doing anything. The גמרא says ירמיה ביראה's ruling already covers this kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: The property of a convert who died without Jewish heirs; it is ownerless and can be acquired by anyone
This is the same as (a known ruling)

phrases.english: If it is with regard to the property of a convert,
this is the same as the ruling of Yirmeya Bira'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְנִכְסֵי הַגֵּר, הַיְינוּ דְּיִרְמְיָה בִּירָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to 'for what purpose?'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the property-law reading of the question as unnecessary.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The answer is already known from ירמיה ביראה's ruling.

steps.title: The turnip seeds case
steps.stepSummary: ירמיה ביראה, quoting רב יהודה, rules that sowing seeds in a convert's land does not acquire it, but plowing a little does.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירמיה ביראה said in the name of רב יהודה: Someone threw turnip seeds into cracks in land that had belonged to a convert. Then another Jew came and plowed it a little. The second person acquires the land. The first person does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source it just mentioned: a case about who acquires a dead convert's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people did something to the land. Plowing counts as an act of acquisition, and sowing seeds into existing cracks does not. The next steps explain why, and that reason connects to our mound case.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר יִרְמְיָה בִּירָאָה אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: As Yirmeya Bira'a said that Rav Yehuda said:
One who threw turnip seeds
into cracks in the land of a convert,
and another Jew came
and plowed in it a little —
the latter acquires; the first does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר יִרְמְיָה בִּירָאָה אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source referred to in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the property-law version of the question is already settled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of ירמיה ביראה in the name of רב יהודה about turnip seeds.

steps.title: Why doesn't the one who sowed acquire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the person who sowed seeds does not acquire the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why sowing does not count as acquiring. This sets up the explanation that links the turnip case to the mound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sowing does eventually improve the land, so it seems it should count. The answer will give the principle that applies to the sunken partitions too.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why sowing seeds does not count as an act of acquisition.

steps.title: An improvement that happens by itself does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: At the moment of sowing nothing improved, and the later improvement happened on its own, so it is not an act of acquisition.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he threw the seeds, the land was not improved. When it did improve, it improved on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that acquisition needs an improvement you make right now, not one that happens later by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing seeds made no visible change in the land at that moment. The growth came later, all by itself. The mound case works the same way: the upper walls become the fence only because the lower walls sank by themselves, so no one acquires the property.
steps.whatToRemember: An act of acquisition must improve the property at the time it is done. Improvement that comes later on its own (מִמֵּילָא) does not acquire.

phrases.english: At the time that he threw the seeds, the land did not improve.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא שָׁבְחָא — מִמֵּילָא קָא מְשַׁבְּחָא.
phrases.english: When it did improve, it improved on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעִידָּנָא דִּשְׁדָא לָא קָא שָׁבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No improvement happened at the moment of sowing, and the later growth happened by itself, so it is not an act of acquisition. The sunken-partition case would follow the same rule.

steps.title: If it is about שבת, it is a partition made on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the second possibility: the question is about carrying on שבת, where the upper walls became a partition on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about שבת. Then this is a partition that was made on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Having set aside the property possibility, the גמרא suggests the question is about שבת. It then describes the case as a partition that came into being on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the lower walls sank, the upper walls did not count as the partition. They became the partition only when the lower walls sank on שבת. So the real question becomes whether a partition formed on שבת counts. That is set up for the ברייתא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition that came into being on שבת

phrases.english: Rather, with regard to Shabbat,
it is a partition made on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting aside the property reading, offers the שבת reading as the other answer to 'for what purpose?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question would be about שבת, where the case is a partition formed on שבת.

steps.title: A partition made on שבת is still a partition
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that any partition made on שבת, accidentally or on purpose, is a valid partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: Any partition made on שבת, whether by accident or on purpose, is called a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the שבת version of the question is also already answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a partition built on purpose on שבת, which is forbidden, still counts as a valid partition. So upper walls that became the partition by themselves surely count, and one may carry in the enclosed קרפף. The question again seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: Both possible reasons for the question seem already answered: for property, by ירמיה ביראה's rule; for שבת, by the ברייתא that a partition made on שבת is valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Making a partition on שבת on purpose is still forbidden. The ברייתא only says that once it exists, it counts as a partition for carrying.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita:
Any partition made on Shabbat,
whether unwittingly or intentionally —
is called a partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא כׇּל מְחִיצָה הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 26 by showing that the שבת reading is already settled.
steps.raayaObject: That a partition formed on שבת, like the upper walls after the lower ones sank, is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: any partition made on שבת, accidentally or on purpose, is a partition.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with step 22, this completes the argument that רבה בר בר חנה's question is unnecessary, since both possible contexts already have answers. Step 28 then challenges the שבת half of this argument.

steps.title: רב נחמן limited the rule about partitions made on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's rule by citing רב נחמן. He said a partition made on שבת counts only to forbid throwing, not to permit carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this ברייתא that רב נחמן said: They only taught this about throwing. But carrying inside it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 26-27. That answer relied on a partition made on שבת being valid, but רב נחמן seems to say it is not fully valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said any partition made on שבת is a partition. רב נחמן explained that this only works as a stringency: you may not throw between it and the public domain. It does not create a full private domain where carrying is allowed, so our case should not be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it said about this? (introduces a challenge from a known teaching)
to throw (from one domain to another)
to carry (move things around inside the area)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'throwing' and 'carrying'. Throwing into or out of the area is forbidden, which is the strict side. Carrying inside is the lenient side, and that is what רב נחמן says is NOT allowed.

phrases.english: Wasn't it said about it,
Rav Nachman said:
They taught this only regarding throwing,
phrases.notes: The partition counts to make throwing forbidden.

phrases.english: but carrying (inside) is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא used in step 27 by citing רב נחמן's limitation of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in steps 26-27 that the שבת version of רבה בר בר חנה's question is already settled by the ברייתא that a partition made on שבת is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a partition made on שבת only counts to forbid throwing and does not permit carrying, it cannot make the area permitted for carrying.

steps.title: רב נחמן's limit is only for a partition built on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן's limit applies only to someone who built the partition on purpose, breaking שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב נחמן's statement was said, it was said about someone who did it on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב נחמן was talking only about a partition built on purpose on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who builds on שבת on purpose has broken שבת, so the חכמים penalized him and forbade carrying there. If the partition came about by accident or by itself, there is no penalty and carrying is allowed. So the answer from step 26 still works.

keyTerms.meaning: When it was said (it was said only about...)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a penalty (קנס) on someone who breaks the law on purpose does not apply to an accident.

phrases.english: When the statement of Rav Nachman was said —
it was said about one who did it on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב נַחְמָן אַמֵּזִיד אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 by limiting רב נחמן's statement to a deliberate act.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the restriction applies only to מזיד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב נחמן forbade carrying inside any partition made on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: He forbade it only as a penalty for building on purpose. A partition made by accident or by itself permits carrying. So the ברייתא does settle the sunken-partition case for שבת, and the question again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A real case: plowing beat building a partition
steps.stepSummary: A woman built a partition on top of a partition in a dead גר's field. A man plowed a little, and רב נחמן gave the field to the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman made a partition on top of a partition in a גר's property. A certain man came and plowed in it a little. He came before רב נחמן, who established the field in the man's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story that matches רב חסדא's ruling in step 15 (a partition on top of a partition does not acquire a convert's property) and the ruling in step 23 that plowing a little does acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר who dies with no heirs leaves ownerless property, and the first to do an act of acquisition (חזקה) gets it. The woman's added partition did not count as acquiring. The man's small amount of plowing improved the land right away, so רב נחמן gave him the field.

keyTerms.meaning: a גר's property (ownerless if he died without heirs)
a partition built on top of another partition
he plowed / broke up the ground
he established it in his possession (ruled it was his)

phrases.english: A certain woman who made
a partition on top of a partition
in the property of a (deceased) convert.
A certain man came,
and plowed in it a little.
He came before Rav Nachman,
who established it in his possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּעֲבַדָה מְחִיצָה עַל גַּבֵּי מְחִיצָה בְּנִכְסֵי הַגֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שבת topic and goes back to the acquisition side (step 15's 'בנכסי הגר לא קנה' and steps 23-25), showing it in a real ruling.
steps.raayaObject: Building a partition in a גר's field does not acquire it, but plowing a little does.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case ruled by רב נחמן.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains to the woman why she lost
steps.stepSummary: The woman protested, and רב נחמן told her she did not take possession the way people normally do.
steps.simpleTranslation: She came and cried out before him. He said to her: What can I do for you? You did not take possession the way people take possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the woman complaining and רב נחמן explaining his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a partition on top of an existing one is not a normal way people take ownership of land. Plowing is a normal act that improves the field. So the act of acquisition must be the kind people usually use.

keyTerms.meaning: What can I do for you?

steps.whatToRemember: To acquire ownerless land you need a normal act of possession that improves the land right away, like plowing. Building a partition on top of a partition does not count.

phrases.english: She came and was crying out before him.
He said to her:
What can I do for you,
since you did not take possession the way people take possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ מַאי אֶיעְבֵּיד לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from step 30 with רב נחמן's reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An act of acquisition must be the normal way people take possession. Her partition was not, so the man who plowed got the field.

steps.title: A yard of three units with one unit roofed: רבא says the roofed part counts
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a קרפף of three בית סאה with one בית סאה roofed. רבא says the roofed part still counts toward the size, so the yard is too big.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קרפף of three בית סאה, and he roofed one בית סאה of it. רבא said: the roofed area adds to its size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic and gives רבא's opinion. The next step will bring the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may carry in a קרפף not made for living in only if it is up to בית סאתים. Here it is three, but one is roofed like a house. רבא says the roof does not separate it, so the yard is still three בית סאה and carrying is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: an enclosed yard or storage area not made for living in
makes it extra (adds to its size)

steps.confusionAlert: 'מייתרו' means the roofed part makes the yard too big. רבא is the strict side here: the roofed area still counts.

phrases.english: A karpef of three (beit se'a),
and he roofed one beit se'a of it.
Rava said:
The space of its roofed area adds to its size.
phrases.notes: So the yard is three בית סאה and carrying is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַרְפֵּף בֵּית שָׁלֹשׁ וְקֵירָה בּוֹ בֵּית סְאָה רָבָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the size limit of a קרפף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The roofed area counts as part of the קרפף, so it is over בית סאתים and carrying is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי זירא says the roofed part does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא disagrees: the roofed area does not add to the yard's size, so carrying is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: the space of its roofed area does not add to its size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite opinion, so now we have a full מחלוקת between רבא and רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא treats the roofed part as separate, like a house. Without it the open yard is only two בית סאה, which is within the limit, so carrying is allowed.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
The space of its roofed area does not add to its size.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר אֵין אֲוִיר קֵירוּיוֹ מְיַיתְּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the dispute opened in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The roofed area does not count toward the קרפף's size, so it stays within בית סאתים and carrying is permitted.

steps.title: Is this the same argument as רב and שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the dispute between רבא and רבי זירא is the same as an earlier dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that רבא and רבי זירא are arguing about the same point that רב and שמואל argued about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a link between the new argument and an older one. This line sets up the next move, where the older dispute will be quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the roofed part of the קרפף still counts toward its size. רבי זירא said the roofed part does not count. The גמרא wonders whether the real question is whether a roof's edge acts like a wall that separates the roofed area from the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say. This introduces a suggestion that the גמרא may later test or reject.

steps.confusionAlert: A line starting with לֵימָא is only a suggestion. It does not mean the גמרא has decided that the two disputes really are the same.

phrases.english: Let us say that Rava and Rabbi Zeira
are arguing about the same dispute as Rav and Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רָבָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the רבא and רבי זירא argument from steps 32 and 33 and asks whether it matches an earlier dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are רבא and רבי זירא simply repeating the argument between רב and שמואל?

steps.title: The older dispute about a porch in a field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute between רב and שמואל about carrying under an אכסדרה that stands in an open field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: about a roofed porch standing in a field, רב said one may carry in the whole porch, and שמואל said one may carry only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the older dispute that it wants to compare to the argument between רבא and רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה has a roof but does not have proper walls. רב treats the whole area under the roof as one enclosed space, so carrying is allowed everywhere inside it. שמואל treats it like open ground, so one may carry only within four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated. This introduces a quoted dispute between אמוראים.
A roofed porch or veranda without proper walls
An open field, which has the status of a כרמלית
Four cubits, the small distance one may carry in an open area

phrases.english: As it was stated: a roofed porch in a field,
Rav said: one may carry in all of it,
and Shmuel said: one may not carry
except within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: אַכְסַדְרָה בְּבִקְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the רב and שמואל dispute that step 34 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: The proposed match between the רבא and רבי זירא dispute and the רב and שמואל dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute of רב and שמואל about an אכסדרה in a field

steps.title: Why רב allows carrying: the roof edge acts as a wall
steps.stepSummary: רב allows carrying in the whole porch because we say the edge of the roof comes down and closes it off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said one may carry in all of it, because we say the edge of the roof goes down and closes off the area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of פי תקרה יורד וסותם, the edge of a roof is treated as if a wall hangs down from it to the ground. That imaginary wall closes off the porch, so it counts as a private area. On this view, a roofed section also becomes its own closed-off space, which matches רבי זירא's view that the roofed part of the קרפף does not add to its size.

keyTerms.meaning: We say, meaning we apply this rule
Goes down and closes off, as if forming a wall

steps.whyThisMatters: פי תקרה יורד וסותם is a key principle in the laws of מחיצות. It is the real question behind both disputes.

phrases.english: Rav said: one may carry in all of it,
because we say the edge of the roof goes down and closes it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִינַן פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning for רב's ruling quoted in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב applies the rule of פי תקרה יורד וסותם, so the area under a roof counts as enclosed.

steps.title: Why שמואל limits carrying: no imaginary wall
steps.stepSummary: שמואל allows only four אמות because we do not say the edge of the roof comes down and closes off the area.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said one may carry only four אמות, because we do not say the edge of the roof goes down and closes off the area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind שמואל's ruling, which completes the comparison it set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not accept the rule of פי תקרה יורד וסותם, so a roof alone creates no wall. On this view, the roofed part of the קרפף is not separated from the rest and still counts toward its size. That matches רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not say, meaning we do not apply this rule

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison works like this. רב applies פי תקרה יורד וסותם, which matches רבי זירא. שמואל does not apply it, which matches רבא.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: one may not carry
except within four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם.
phrases.english: because we do not say the edge of the roof goes down and closes it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אָמְרִינַן פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reasoning, for שמואל, right after רב's reasoning in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל rejects the rule of פי תקרה יורד וסותם, so a roof alone does not create an enclosure.
